Needs changes before merge. Four geometry defects remain.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. All builds and tests ran locally. I tested the trial merge with upstream/main `211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6`.
I checked the laws from that main commit, not from the PR branch. No golden file changed. No UI file changed, so screenshots are not required.

### Requested before merge

1. **Keep the chord bound when you remove short curve segments.** [`crates/geometry/src/svg/emit.rs:60`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/b5eab805d383335f2bb50c85a427735b518fa997/crates/geometry/src/svg/emit.rs#L60)

   On a 1 mm square page with `viewBox="0 0 1 1"`, import `<path d="M0 0 Q0 0.02 0.02 0"/>`.
   Both inner vertices are removed. The reader emits one line from `(0, 1)` to `(0.02, 1)`.
   The true curve midpoint is `(0.005, 0.99)`. Its distance from that line is 0.01 mm, twice the stated 0.005 mm bound.
   `SketchData::from_dxf` accepts this result as one open chain, with no rejected chain.
   Keep the vertices that the chord bound needs, or refuse the curve by name. Add a pin for this case.

2. **Refuse a curve when its required segment count exceeds the cap.** [`crates/geometry/src/svg/emit.rs:75`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/b5eab805d383335f2bb50c85a427735b518fa997/crates/geometry/src/svg/emit.rs#L75)

   `segments` clamps the count to 20,000. The ellipse branch does the same at line 133.
   This returns geometry that can exceed the chord bound, without a diagnostic.
   With a 100,000,000 mm square page and the same numeric viewBox, import `<path d="M0 0 Q0 100000000 100000000 0"/>`.
   The reader accepts it and emits 20,000 lines.
   At `t = 0.500025`, the true curve is about 0.124994 mm from the nearest emitted line.
   The stated bound is 0.005 mm. Return an import budget error when the required count exceeds the cap. Add a pin for this refusal.

3. **Apply the symbol viewport before you draw its children.** [`crates/geometry/src/svg/walk.rs:141`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/b5eab805d383335f2bb50c85a427735b518fa997/crates/geometry/src/svg/walk.rs#L141)

   On a 100 mm square page with `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`, define this symbol and reference:

   ```xml
   <defs>
     <symbol id="s" viewBox="0 0 10 10"><rect width="10" height="10"/></symbol>
   </defs>
   <use xlink:href="#s" width="50" height="50"/>
   ```

   The probe declares the SVG and XLink namespaces on the root.
   This must produce a 50 by 50 mm square. The reader produces a 10 by 10 mm square and reports no skipped content.
   The symbol branch ignores its viewBox and the use width and height.
   SVG 1.1 gives a referenced symbol a viewport with the use dimensions. See the [W3C use rules](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/struct.html#UseElement).
   Apply that mapping and preserveAspectRatio, or refuse the unsupported case by name. Add a size pin.

4. **Bound the work of reference expansion.** [`crates/geometry/src/svg/walk.rs:126`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/b5eab805d383335f2bb50c85a427735b518fa997/crates/geometry/src/svg/walk.rs#L126)

   The walker does not charge group or use visits to a work budget.
   A six-level graph with ten references at each level makes 1,111,111 group visits.
   The probe has fewer than 100 XML elements. It succeeds with `max_entities = 100` and `max_vertices = 10`.
   Its summary counts only the one rectangle after the graph.
   A fifteen-level version still fits the use-depth guard. The code would visit its empty groups about 10^15 times.
   This is a finite graph, so the loop guard does not stop it. An import can appear to hang on a small file.
   Add a total budget for the traversal work. Check it before each expansion and refuse excess work by name. Pin an acyclic graph with shared references.

### Local results

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` selected the batch tier because geometry changed.
The gate completed in 43.4 minutes: 1,016 steps passed and one failed. Clippy with `-D warnings` passed.
The failed test also fails alone on both the trial merge and the pinned upstream/main commit:

```text
a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation
panicked at crates/app/tests/default_machine_missing.rs:160:5:
the mounted operation has its own machine:
camcraft-cli: post: post blocked - machine of Setup2 for Face2: the default machine file 3axis-vmc.mch cannot be read
```

The last line is the diagnostic prefix. Its remaining text names the temporary asset directory.
This is a baseline failure, separate from the four SVG findings above.

No fixture directory changed. No new STEP fixture needs a step_agreement row.

### Mutations run by this review

I used copies under `/tmp` of the SVG module and its original SVG tests. The harness redirects the SVG import to that copy.
It uses the real geometry crate for the shared document and sketch types. The PR source stayed unchanged.

| Mutation | Pin | Changed | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remove the Y reflection | `svg_rectangle_with_a_hole_in_mm_nests_and_flips_y` | FAIL | PASS |
| Disable the unit refusal for a sized file | `svg_without_a_physical_size_is_never_guessed` | FAIL | PASS |

The nine original SVG tests passed before the mutations and after restoration.
All copied module files match the PR source again.
The separate geometry probes reproduce all four findings above. No review evidence was committed.

It reached all motion and app heavy targets. All 234 steps passed in 38.3 minutes.
The gate checked the two declared known-fail motion tests. Each failed at its expected assertion, as required.
The full shared face finish suite passed all six tests. The reached light twins ran with the ignored tests.

- The import uses the shared sketch entity and undo history. The MCP tool and script verb call the command.
- `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs` grew by one line and now has 495 lines. This size note is not blocking.
- The posted golden for an SVG profile remains deferred to #3042, as the body states. This review did not exercise that path.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
